newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Aug 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Aug 6.

text.p: THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

A decision by the High Court yesterday to strike down State petrol, alcohol and tobacco levies has been met with calls from business and State leaders for wide-ranging tax reform, and a review of Commonwealth-State financial arrangements. The High Court' decision will have a dramatic impact on State revenue. Page 1.

A new industry-wide national trust fund to be announced by the Federal Government today will see at least A$1.5 billion in aged care accommodation bonds brought into the financial system. The scheme should allow about A$130 million in funds to be generated for nursing homes. Page 3.

In a move reflecting the Federal Government's need to tackle its mid-term blues and take the initiative on a social issue of major concern to the community, Prime Minister John Howard has suggested State premiers gather at a national 'summit' in October to discuss domestic violence. Page 3.

Queensland Premier Rob Borbidge will continue with his overhaul of the Criminal Justice Commission despite a ruling by the State's Supreme Court that the current Connolly-Ryan inquiry is politically biased. The current inquiry was ordered while the CJC was investigating allegations of electoral bribery. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Federal Government has agreed to collect new national taxes in response to a High Court decision that has declared as unconstitutional the States' ability to collect taxes on alcohol, petrol and tobacco, and has left a large hole in the States' revenue. The decision has sparked further calls for a goods and services tax and a rejig of Federal-State financial relations. Page 1.

Australian athlete Cathy Freeman said she was "a very proud girl" after winning the 400 metres event at the world athletics championships in Athens. Freeman took her victory lap with both an Australian and Aboriginal flag, and said she was proud of being both Australian and Aboriginal, something she explained as being "two and the same". Page 1.

A single photo taken by Sydney paramedic James Porter has snapped the moment when 27-year-old ski instructor Stuart Diver emerged almost unharmed from the rubble of the Thredbo landslide. Porter took the photo spontaneously, and said it was only after th event that he realised he had captured a pictorial frame of history. Page 1.

Queensland Premier Rob Borbidge has vowed to overhaul the State's Criminal Justice Commission after the Queensland Supreme Court ruled yesterday the controversial A$11 million inquiry into the anti-corruption body was riddled with bias, and ordered it to be closed. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Federal Government has said it will introduce a uniform national tax on petrol, alcohol and tobacco, after the High Court ruled yesterday State taxes on these products were unconstitutional. The insistence by Federal Treasurer Peter Costello that there will be no price rises could also be unconstitutional. Page 1.

Federal Education Minister Amanda Vanstone said yesterday the Federal Government would set aside funds to encourage universities to drop the system of accepting students based on their tertiary entrance ranking. Vanstone described the ranking as grossly unfair and unreliable. Page 1.

Australian athlete Cathy Freeman, the new world 400 metres champion, said it is her wish that her efforts would help unite black and white Australians. Freeman held both the Australian and Aboriginal flags aloft after her race, and said she is proud of who she is - an Australian Aborigine. Page 1.

The Industry Commission has recommended, in its submission to the Federal Government's review of higher education, that the Higher Education Contribution Scheme needs to be overhauled, and suggests the higher education funding system is inequitable, stifles competition, and disallows students from shopping around to find the best course. Page 3.
THE AGE

In a 4-3 majority, the High Court yesterday ruled that the States are unable to charge franchise fees on cigarettes because they are an excise duty and therefore unconstitutional. The decision has implications for similar State taxes on alcohol and cigarettes, and could see the Federal Government delivering a rescue tax package for the States. Page 1.

Australian athlete Cathy Freeman yesterday became the first Aborigine, and the first Australian woman to win a track world title, after winning the 400 metres at the World Athletics titles in Athens. The result has come at a time that Freeman describes as having been physically, emotionally and mentally testing. Page 1.

The New South Wales Ambulance Service yesterday released a photograph of the rescue of Stuart Diver, the only survivor of the Thredbo landslide. The photo, taken after Diver had spent 60 hours under the rubble, was released as a tribute to Diver's extraordinary will to survive. Page 1.

The Victorian Government last night shut down four suburban train lines in response to a "go-slow" by workers which side-lined a quarter of the city's train fleet. The Government has also quit talks with unions planned for today, and has sacked 22 equipment examiners for working too slowly. Page 1.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
